record.context_brief: Existence of omega plus below two
record.original_question: For m >= 3 and numbers 1, theta_1, ..., theta_m linearly independent over Z, define omega_+(Theta) from approximation of the linear form theta_1 x_1 + ... + theta_m x_m by positive integers x_i. Does there exist such a collection with omega_+(Theta) < 2? The paper explicitly asks this first for m = 3 and then suggests the same possibility for arbitrary m.

evidence.quote: We are interested in small values of the linear form ||θ1 x1 + ... + θm xm || in positive integers x1 , ..., xn . Put ψ+ (t) = min ||θ1 x1 + ... + θm xm ||.

3. As it was shown behind for θ1 , ..., θm , m ⩾ 3 linearly independent over Z together with 1 it may happen (49). But in view of Theorem 18 I may conjecture that for m = 3 (or even for an arbitrary m) there exist a collection of linearly independent numbers 1, θ1 , ..., θm such that ω+ (Θ) < 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m \ge 3$ be an integer, and let $\Theta = (\theta_1, \dots, \theta_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m$ be such that $1, \theta_1, \dots, \theta_m$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Z}$. For a real number $\xi$, denote by $\|\xi\|$ the distance from $\xi$ to the nearest integer. Define the function
$$\psi_+(t) \;=\; \min \bigl\{\, \|\theta_1 x_1 + \theta_2 x_2 + \cdots + \theta_m x_m\| \;:\; x_1,\dots,x_m \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0},\ \max_i x_i \le t\,\bigr\}$$
for $t \ge 1$, and define the (ordinary) Diophantine exponent in positive integers
$$\omega_+(\Theta) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\, \gamma > 0 \;:\; \liminf_{t\to\infty} t^{\gamma} \psi_+(t) < \infty\,\bigr\}.$$
Question: Does there exist a tuple $\Theta = (\theta_1,\dots,\theta_m)$ with $1,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_m$ linearly independent over $\mathbb{Z}$ such that
$$\omega_+(\Theta) < 2\,?$$
Settle this first in the case $m = 3$, and more generally for arbitrary $m \ge 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a published resolution of the question of whether there exists $\Theta$ with $1,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_m$ linearly independent over $\mathbb{Z}$ ($m\ge 3$) and $\omega_+(\Theta) < 2$. Related work by Moshchevitin (e.g., on Diophantine approximation with positive integers, refining a theorem of W.M. Schmidt) treats analogous problems but does not appear to settle this specific conjecture. Status appears to remain unknown based on available sources.

status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including conjectures on omega_+ for linear forms in positive integers.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as a conjecture/open problem in a list of open problems in Diophantine approximation.

status_evidence.title: On Diophantine approximations with positive integers: a remark to W.M. Schmidt's theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Moshchevitin's work generalizing Schmidt's theorem on approximation by linear forms in positive integers.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist on approximation by linear forms in positive integers, but do not resolve the omega_+ < 2 question.

status_evidence.title: Exponents of Diophantine approximation (survey, Bugeaud)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of exponents of Diophantine approximation; standard exponents discussed without resolution of the positive-integer variant omega_+.
status_evidence.claim: Survey on Diophantine exponents does not record a resolution of this particular question.
